scope: Supplemental independent source review of the coverage-only release-profile repair; prior approval and failed-run evidence remain unchanged.
observed_diff: Instrumented cargo test adds --release, retaining --all-targets and --include-ignored.
Instrumented capture executes the binary from the same isolated target/release directory.
llvm-cov report adds --release to select the same instrumented profile.
A focused test requires exactly one test/build/report command with the release flag, the release capture path, the isolated target, and the complete test selection.
reasoning: The four workflow changes make all coverage stages use one profile. They address the recorded debug-profile timeout without removing tests, extending bounds, or changing production source.
Coverage remains qualification-only in an isolated target and subshell. Ordinary source tests and ordinary release capture qualification are unchanged.
The 300-second test, 300-second build and 180-second live-capture limits remain unchanged. A timeout or failure still prevents sealing a sender artifact.
Ordinary release hashes are checked before coverage and again after success or failure. The instrumented binaries are not packaged as sender binaries.
The percentage remains a report-only observation. Optimized-profile coverage must be identified as such and is not interchangeable with historical debug-profile coverage.

failure_evidence_reviewed.interpretation: The retained diagnosis supports profile correction. Timeout without an assertion failure does not establish that the unfinished test passes.

verification_boundary.new_linux_runtime_qualification: NOT_RUN at review time; fresh exact-source producer required
